# Results -- Study 253 (Wiki-Views) on the offline best-effort real tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Recipe: each
month-end, rank the basket by its **attention surge** -- the month-over-month
log change in the company's Wikipedia page-views (curated anchors expanded to a
monthly panel) -- long the bottom-surge (attention-drought) quintile, short the
top-surge quintile (the Da-Engelberg-Gao 2011 reversal prior), hold 1 month and
rebalance. Pinned against a random-portfolio control of the same leg size.
**Survivorship-biased**: the basket is a fixed mega-cap set of current survivors
projected backwards -- all results are upper bounds.*

**Important data honesty note.** The Wikimedia pageviews REST API only covers
2015-07 onward, is rate-limited, and the raw monthly series is dominated by
one-off news spikes. Rather than ship a brittle live scrape, the page-view side
is a **curated anchor table** (`data.WIKI_VIEWS_ANCHORS`) expanded
deterministically into a monthly panel. The closest-to-real run below joins
those curated views to a realistic equity-return panel generated **independently
of the page-views** (`data.best_effort_real_tape`) -- which is the honest null,
because curated mega-cap page-views carry no causal link to next-month prices.
When a genuine yfinance cache is present, `verify.py --fetch` re-runs the same
machinery against the real Yahoo monthly tape. As-of **2026-06-17**.

## Data stamp

| Source | Window | Shape | Fingerprint (last row) |
|--------|--------|-------|----------------------|
| Curated Wikipedia anchors -> monthly panel | 2016-01-31 -> 2025-12-31 | 120 months x 30 tickers | `cbc685eb52db` |
| Best-effort returns (offline proxy, views-independent) | 2016-01-31 -> 2025-12-31 | 120 months x 30 tickers | `1552feb23616` |

Universe: ~30 mega-cap names; quintile cut (`q = 0.20`) -> ~6 names per leg.

## Primary specification (low-minus-high surge quintile, 1-month hold)

| Portfolio | Mean return | HAC *t* |
|-----------|------------|---------|
| Low-surge (attention drought, long leg) | +14.1%/yr | +2.44 |
| High-surge (attention surge, short leg) | +15.3%/yr | +2.91 |
| Equal-weight basket | +14.5%/yr | -- |
| **Spread (low - high)** | **-1.2%/yr = -10.2 bps/mo** | **-0.31** |
| Low-surge excess over basket | -0.4%/yr | -0.14 |

- The drought-minus-surge **spread HAC *t* = -0.31** -- indistinguishable from
  zero. The reversal story does **not** appear on this tape; if anything the
  high-surge leg edges ahead (the opposite of the prior, also insignificant).
- The block-bootstrap 95% CI on the spread Sharpe (ann) is **[-0.73, +0.54]**
  (63% of resamples negative) -- straddling zero, as a null should.
- The random-portfolio null is centred at zero (-3.6 bps/mo mean across 200
  draws per month), confirming there is no cross-sectional information in the
  curated surge signal once joined to independent prices.

## Sub-period analysis -- nothing to persist

| Period | Spread/yr | HAC *t* | n months |
|--------|-----------|---------|----------|
| 2017-2019 | -2.5%/yr | -0.34 | 36 |
| 2020-2022 | +0.3%/yr | +0.04 | 36 |
| 2023-2026 | -0.3%/yr | -0.03 | 35 |

No sub-period clears |t| = 1, let alone the t = 2 inference bar. There is no
signal to decay because there was none to begin with on this tape.

## Tradability -- turnover and cost drag

The attention-surge ranking churns hard: roughly **89%** average monthly
two-leg turnover (page-view surges are noisy and reshuffle the legs each month).

| One-way cost | Monthly drag | Net spread | Net *t* |
|-------------|-------------|------------|---------|
| 10 bps | 35.6 bps/mo | -45.8 bps/mo = -5.5%/yr | -1.39 |

Even before borrow on the short leg, the gross spread is already negative; costs
only deepen the loss. There is nothing to trade.

## Positive control -- the machinery finds attention-reversal when planted

On the deterministic synthetic tape (`data.synthetic_attention_panel`) the same
quintile engine recovers a planted attention-reversal premium monotonically:

| Planted premium | Spread mean/yr | Spread t-stat |
|----------------|---------------|--------------|
| 0.00 (null)    | -4.4%/yr (chance) | -1.21 (null) |
| +0.02          | +62.0%/yr     | +17.03       |

The engine works -- it lights up strongly when the reversal effect is real. The
best-effort real tape simply has no such effect.

## Verdict

- **Signal -- NONE.** Drought-minus-surge spread HAC *t* = -0.31; no sub-period
  clears |t| = 1; the random-portfolio null is centred at zero. The Da-
  Engelberg-Gao attention prior has literature support, but our offline tape --
  curated page-views joined to realistic prices -- shows **no** forward
  information. Literature support alone never earns more than WEAK, and here even
  the sign is wrong, so the signal is **NONE**. (A genuine Wikimedia-vs-prices
  cache could be re-run via `verify.py --fetch`; published attention effects are
  intraday-to-weekly and tiny, not a tradable monthly mega-cap spread.)
- **Tradability -- MIRAGE.** A gross spread that is negative, ~89% monthly
  turnover, and a short leg that pays borrow: there is no edge to harvest and
  costs make a negative number worse. **MIRAGE**.
- **Survivorship -- named.** The basket is current mega-cap survivors projected
  backwards; all results are upper bounds, and the upper bound is already zero.
